title: Sayonara, Zetsubou-Sensei
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Nozomu Itoshiki is a deeply pessimistic, openly suicidal schoolteacher whose class is full of exaggerated students: a stalker, a shut-in, an obsessive-compulsive, a girl who arrives with unexplained bruises, and Kafuka, a relentless optimist. Each episodic chapter uses his despair as black comedy to satirize Japanese society, media and everyday absurdities.
life_message: Laughing at despair and social absurdity can expose what is wrong with the world, though the series offers satire more than answers.

folkways.japan: The satire targets Japanese social customs, media and politics, and draws on prewar literary imagery of the despairing intellectual.

delivery.evidence: ANN's Brienza: masterful satire voiced through Itoshiki's exaggerated, histrionic rants; comic, not preachy.
delivery.note: Social commentary is stated outright in comic rants, and both despair and optimism are mocked.

winners_losers: No one wins outright; Kafuka's optimism and Itoshiki's despair are both mocked, and social absurdities take the most hits.
